external_entities.name: Decentralized Application
external_entities.description: Web application requesting batched call execution via JSON-RPC
external_entities.trust_rationale: DApps can send arbitrary JSON-RPC requests; all inputs must be validated for schema, capabilities, chain support, and user approval required

external_entities.name: Wallet User
external_entities.description: Human user who approves or rejects transaction batches
external_entities.trust_rationale: User is the ultimate authority for their wallet but may not understand technical details; approval is required gate for all operations

external_entities.name: Ethereum Blockchain
external_entities.description: The blockchain network where calls are executed
external_entities.trust_rationale: Blockchain execution is deterministic and verifiable but subject to MEV, reorgs, and network conditions

external_entities.name: Fingerprinting Attacker
external_entities.description: Malicious actor attempting to identify wallet type via capability responses
external_entities.trust_rationale: Explicit attacker entity; wallet must filter capabilities to prevent fingerprinting and privacy leakage

external_entities.name: Block Producer (Miner)
external_entities.description: Entity producing new blocks that need difficulty calculation
external_entities.trust_rationale: Block producers have economic stake in valid blocks; their difficulty claims are verified independently

external_entities.name: Network Peer
external_entities.description: P2P peer sending block headers for validation
external_entities.trust_rationale: Network peers can broadcast any block header; all headers must be independently validated for difficulty

external_entities.name: P2P Peer Node
external_entities.description: Other Ethereum nodes broadcasting blocks over the P2P network
external_entities.trust_rationale: Peer nodes can broadcast blocks under any ruleset; nodes must validate against appropriate fork rules based on block number

external_entities.name: EIP Author
external_entities.description: External party proposing and championing an EIP through the process
external_entities.trust_rationale: Authors are authenticated through GitHub but their proposals still require editor review, community consensus, and security review

external_entities.name: EIP Editor
external_entities.description: Repository maintainer who validates and merges EIP submissions
external_entities.trust_rationale: Editors are trusted gatekeepers but operate under defined impartiality rules; they validate format not merit

external_entities.name: Ethereum Core Developers
external_entities.description: Client implementation teams who review and implement Core EIPs
external_entities.trust_rationale: Core developers are authenticated and have implementation responsibility; they build rough consensus for protocol changes

misclassified_entities.name: Block Processor
misclassified_entities.description: Node component processing blocks for chain updates
misclassified_entities.reason: Block Processor is an internal node component, not an external entity. It is part of the local node's execution engine that processes blocks, not an external actor sending data into the system.

coverage_analysis.notes: EXT-USER and EXT-BLOCKCHAIN are context entities affecting state transitions but without explicit incoming edges. EXT-ATTACKER is a threat actor referenced in security context. EXT-AUTHOR, EXT-EIP-EDITOR, and EXT-CORE-DEVS operate in governance process without explicit data flow edges. EIP-7523 has no external entities (all internal state validation).
